Ind. Code  ch. 8-1-26  provides  the  procedure for  the Indiana  Utility  Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations  of said  chapter. Upon 
review of  those findings,  the Indiana  Underground  Plant  Protection Advisory  Committee

Case.   
The Cases received pursuant to Ind. Code ch. 8-1- 26 and ripe for Commiss ion action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
Pursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations  to the 
Commission. The Commission  UPHOLDS the findings  of violations  by  the Pipeline  Safety 
Division and APPROVES  the recommendations  of the Advisory  Committee  as  listed on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to  the Division  is directed  to prepare  and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
Any approve d civil penalt ies are due withi n 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
Any approved trainings must be comple ted no late r than 180 day s from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
IT IS SO ORDERED.

input.command: cd /tmp/r2run-6wes7ybx/data/text; grep -ho "IC 8-1-26-[^ ]*([a-zA-Z-]\{2,\})" *.txt | sort | uniq -c; grep -c "RecommendationForm" *.txt | awk -F: '{s+=$2}END{print s}'; grep -c "finds the following" *.txt | awk -F: '{s+=$2}END{print s}'

cd /tmp/r2run-6wes7ybx/data/text; cat > $TMPDIR/a.py <<'E'
import re,glob,collections
res=collections.defaultdict(lambda:[0,0]);n=0;nocite=0;odd=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.txt')):
    t=open(f).read()
    parts=re.split(r'finds\s+the\s+following\s+violation\(s\)\s*:',t)[1:]
    for p in parts:
        n+=1
        m=re.search(r'IC\s*8-1-26-\s*(\S+)',p)
        if not m: nocite+=1;odd.append((f,p[:100]));continue
        cite=m.group(1)
        q=re.search(r'\(([A-Za-z-]{2,})\)$',cite)
        pm=re.split(r'recommends\s+the\s+following\s+civil\s+penalty\s*:',p)
        rec=pm[1] if len(pm)>1 else ''
        rec=re.split(r'Abstentions',rec)[0]
        d=re.search(r'\$+\s*([\d, ]*\d)',rec)
        amt=float(d.group(1).replace(' ','').replace(',','')) if d else 0
        if q:
            r=res[q.group(1)];r[0]+=1;r[1]+= (amt==0)
print(n,nocite,odd[:3])
for k,v in res.items():print(k,v,round(100*v[1]/v[0],1))
E
python3 -I $TMPDIR/a.py

Among cases with each qualifier, the share with a $0 headline penalty is:

| Qualifier | Cases | Headline penalty $0 | Percentage |
|---|---|---|---|
| expire | 517 | 184 | **35.6%** |
| prior | 271 | 58 | **21.4%** |
| out | 191 | 35 | **18.3%** |

I read these from the text files of all 58 orders, and I counted the "finds the following violation(s)" blocks to get the case totals.

- **Garbled cites:** The text extraction sometimes misread the cite, for example "8-l-26" in place of "8-1-26". I allowed for that.
- **Cites missing from the text:** Six cases have no cite in the text at all. I couldn't classify them, and I didn't check the PDFs. If any of them carries one of these three qualifiers, the counts above would be slightly off.
- **"Training or $5,000" cases:** Where a recommendation reads like "Training or $5,000 if respondent fails to complete training," the headline penalty is $5,000, because that is the first dollar amount printed.
- **Count mismatch:** I found 9,951 case blocks, but the text has only 9,965 "Case Number" lines and 7,825 "RecommendationForm" headers. The mismatch suggests the extraction is not perfectly clean, so treat the percentages as very close rather than certain.
